'''Izabella Łaba''' (born 1966)<ref>Birth date from {{citation
 | last = Wolff | first = Thomas H.
 | editor1-last = Łaba | editor1-first = Izabella
 | editor2-last = Shubin | editor2-first = Carol
 | isbn = 0-8218-3449-5
 | location = Providence, RI
 | mr = 2003254
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | series = University Lecture Series
 | title = Lectures on harmonic analysis
 | volume = 29
 | year = 2003}}, [https://books.google.com/books?id=i56jcHMvXuUC&pg=PR4 Library of Congress Cataloging-in-Publication Data], p.&nbsp;iv.</ref> is a Polish-Canadian mathematician, a professor of [[mathematics]] at the [[University of British Columbia]]. Her main research specialties are [[harmonic analysis]], [[geometric measure theory]], and [[additive combinatorics]].

==Professional career==
Łaba earned a master's degree in 1986 from the [[University of Wrocław]].<ref name="cj"/> She received her PhD from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1994, under the supervision of [[Israel Michael Sigal]],<ref name="cj"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=16070|name=Izabella Laba}}</ref> after which she was a postdoctoral scholar at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] and then an assistant professor at [[Princeton University]] before moving to UBC in 2000.<ref name="cj"/>

She is one of three founding editors of the ''Online Journal of Analytic Combinatorics''.<ref>[http://www.math.rochester.edu/ojac/editors.html Editorial board], ''Online Journal of Analytic Combinatorics'', retrieved 2013-01-28.</ref>

==Contributions==
Łaba's thesis research proved the asymptotic completeness of many [[n-body problem|n-body systems]] in the presence of a constant magnetic field.<ref name="cj"/><ref name="kn"/> While at UCLA, with [[Nets Katz]] and [[Terence Tao]], she made important contributions to the theory of [[Kakeya set]]s, including the best known [[lower bound]] on these sets in three-dimensional Euclidean spaces.<ref name="cj"/><ref name="kn"/> Her more recent work concerns [[harmonic analysis]], [[periodic tiling]]s, and [[Falconer's conjecture]] on sets of distances of points.<ref name="kn"/>

==Awards and honours==
Łaba was the 2004 winner of the [[Coxeter–James Prize]], an annual prize of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] for outstanding young mathematicians.<ref name="cj">[http://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2004/res-prizes CMS 2004 Coxeter-James Prize: Dr. Izabella Łaba (University of British Columbia)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180216143808/https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2004/res-prizes |date=2018-02-16 }}, [[Canadian Mathematical Society]], retrieved 2013-01-28.</ref> In 2008, the CMS honoured her again with their [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]], given to an outstanding woman in mathematics.<ref name="kn">[http://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2007/res-prizes.html CMS 2008 Krieger-Nelson Prize:	 Dr. Izabella Łaba (University of British Columbia)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180216143810/https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2007/res-prizes.html |date=2018-02-16 }}, retrieved 2013-01-28.</ref>

In 2012 she became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-01-27.</ref>, and in 2016 she was the Etta Z. Falconer lecturer for the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Falconer Lectures |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/falconer-lectures/ |access-date=2026-04-10 |website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) |language=en-US}}</ref>
